newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end tad higher in brisk trading.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end tad higher in brisk trading.

text.p: Argentine stocks pared early gains to close only fractionally higher Tuesday.
But the market was seen keeping its positive edge thanks to fresh institutional bidding which restored volume to healthy levels, dealers said.

"The bolsa performed well today, although the tone is rather subdued and deals are very selective," said Jose Napoli of Ignoto y Napoli traders. "Nobody rushes to buy -- they take their time and step in strictly when it's convenient."
The blue-chip MerVal index slipped off a high of 712.38 and closed up 0.1 percent at 708.02.
The index, which rose 0.6 percent Monday and 1.5 percent last week, was seen facing mild resistance at 710-715.
Players took Tuesday's Treasury bill launch, which fetched much lower-than-expected rates, in their stride.

"The news is completely in accordance with Argentina's successful global bond launch (in January) -- basically financing conditions are excellent and this was underscored by January's strong tax collection," another trader said.
Floor volume swelled to a strong 31.8 million pesos from 21.4 million Monday, while over-the-counter turnover picked up to 107.1 million pesos from 79.5 million Monday.
The broad market index closed up 0.6 percent Tuesday, with winners outstripping losers 39 to 18 and 20 issues closing flat.
Top main-tier performers were Bansud bank, holding company Comercial del Plata and real estate developer Irsa, which rallied 4.1 percent, 2.8 percent and 2.5 percent, respectively.
MerVal decliners were led by carmaker Ciadea and construction stock Polledo, both down 2.0 percent, and petrochemical concern Indupa, off 1.9 percent.
